keywords.meaning: Logical opposite of the design intent
Only some of the design intent is achieved
Relative to the clock time; synchronous function waiting for infinite time / async function delayed notification; deadlock and starvation
Changing in quantity or unstable; not following periodicity
Complete substitution; another activity takes place
None of the design intent is achieved
Relative to data message transmission / execution sequence (e.g., DeInit called before Init)
When it cannot be mapped to any of the above

definitions.name: Memory Interference
definitions.dfi: Common code sharing data; protect against / detect unauthorized access (illegal writes) to ASIL data.
definitions.description: If a module function/API/method is used in multiple execution contexts (threads), data corruption may occur. Such executions must be analyzed. Data may be inconsistent due to concurrency and re-entrancy. Data inconsistency may occur during context switching.
example_safety_mechanisms_measures: Follow safety analysis and provide recommendation/restriction to the user

definitions.name: Timing and Execution Interference
definitions.description: Timing and execution blocking/delay in higher ASIL application due to lower ASIL / QM application. Includes deadlocks and livelocks.
failure_mode_examples: Higher ASIL application waiting for lower ASIL / QM application to complete their actions
example_safety_mechanisms_measures: Runtime profiling and setting appropriate priorities to processes/threads

definitions.name: Exchange of Information
definitions.dfi: Applicable for safety critical communication between components.
definitions.description: Applicable for safety critical communication between (a) ARA component and daemon of a functional cluster and (b) two functional clusters (e.g., STM-EXM, PHM-STM). Failure modes include repetition, loss, delay, or corruption of information.
example_safety_mechanisms_measures: Distinction between on-board and off-board communications (co-located vs remote)
